limitations: All 226 entries are source-syntax candidates, not resolved Express routes; mount paths and middleware behavior are not resolved.
A string literal entry records a candidate method and path only. Regex and dynamic-expression entries are clearly marked and are not exact-path coverage.
Middleware argument counts are syntax hints only; they do not establish authentication, authorization, validation, or response behavior.
A generic Go 501 fallback is not evidence that the upstream route returns 501 or that the route is handled correctly.
A passing executable case samples only its listed request shape and fixture state. CompatibilityStatus remains unverified for every route until explicit review of relevant variants.
Query, body, permission, content-type, image-cache, and error variants are separate behaviors and are not implied by a path match.

falsePositiveInventory.risk: ApiRouter, PublicRouter, HlsRouter and Auth mount prefixes can be nested or runtime-configured; the extractor does not resolve them.
The middleware argument count does not reveal permission checks or whether a handler returns early.
A regex path can match many concrete paths and is not one exact route.
A computed path may be incomplete or may expand into multiple routes.
The experimental server's fallback can hide missing handler integration during manual probing; compare only against source-executed upstream responses.
One cover path can vary by raw mode, format, dimensions, cache headers and response bytes.
Network-backed provider routes need separate mock-backed and live-network test categories; neither implies the other.
